partners.diseaseBName: methylmalonic acidemia due to transcobalamin receptor defect
partners.mechanism_chain: ABCD4 (HGNC:28521) —DISRUPTS→ cobalamin (vitamin B12) uptake and transport (GO:0015079); CD320 (HGNC:23322) —DISRUPTS→ cobalamin (vitamin B12) uptake and transport (GO:0015079); cobalamin (vitamin B12) uptake and transport (GO:0015079) —DECREASES→ methylmalonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17508); cobalamin (vitamin B12) uptake and transport (GO:0015079) —DECREASES→ homocysteine (CHEBI:17998); methylmalonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17508) —LEADS_TO→ developmental delay (HP:0001263); methylmalonyl-CoA (CHEBI:17508) —LEADS_TO→ failure to thrive (HP:0011400); ABCD4 (HGNC:28521) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0000422); CD320 (HGNC:23322) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0000422); lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ developmental delay (HP:0001263); lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0000422) —LEADS_TO→ failure to thrive (HP:0011400). Mutations in ABCD4 (involved in lysosomal degradation) and CD320 (transcobalamin receptor for vitamin B12 uptake) both impair the cellular availability and function of vitamin B12. This deficiency disrupts essential metabolic pathways, including the conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine. The accumulation of methylmalonyl-CoA and the deficiency in methionine contribute to downstream effects leading to developmental delay and failure to thrive. Both genes converge on the shared pathways of vitamin B12 transport/utilization and lysosomal degradation, impacting multiple downstream processes.
